==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology 1===
{{etymon|en|id=look|:inh|enm:peren<id:peer><ety:inh<ang:*pȳran>>|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|peren}}, {{m|enm|pyren}}, {{m|enm|piren|t=to peer, gaze}}, perhaps from {{inh|en|ang|*pȳran|t=to look, peer}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*pūrijan|t=to look}}, related to {{cog|stq|pierje|t=to look}}, {{cog|nds-nl|piren|t=to look}}, {{cog|vls|pieren|t=to look with narrowed eyes, squint at}}, {{cog|nl|pieren|t=to look closely at, examine}}, {{cog|enm|pouren|t=to gaze, look closely}}, {{cog|en|pore|t=to study meticulously}}. Compare also {{cog|fy|pluere|t=to peer}}, {{cog|nl|pluren|t=to gaze squintingly}}, {{cog|nds-de|plieren|t=to blink}}, {{cog|da|plire|t=to peer}}, {{cog|sv|plira}}, {{m|sv|blira|t=to peer}}, and thence ultimately related to the root of {{cog|en|blear}}. 

The sense meaning "to be visible" is perhaps from a shortening of {{m|en|appear}}.<ref>{{R:Online_Etymology_Dictionary|peer}}</ref><ref>{{R:Lexico}}</ref><ref>{{R:AHD}}</ref>

====Alternative forms====
* {{alt|en|pire|pyre||obsolete or dialectal}}

====Pronunciation====
* {{IPA|en|/pɪə/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/pɪː/|/pɪjə/|a=SSB}}
* {{enPR|pîr|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/pɪɹ/}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-peer.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/piə̯/|a=NZ}}
* {{IPA|en|/piɾ/|a=Scotland}}
* {{IPA|en|/pɛː/|a=East Anglia,near-square}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪə(ɹ)|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|pier|;|pair|pare|pear<aa:all <<near-square>>>}}

====Verb====
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[look]] with [[difficulty]], or as if [[search]]ing for something.
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|act=I|scene=i|passage={{...}} I should be still / Plucking the grass, to know where sits the wind, / '''Peering''' in maps for ports, and piers, and roads;}}
#* '''1798''', {{w|Samuel Taylor Coleridge}}, ''{{w|The Rime of the Ancient Mariner}}'' in ''{{w|Lyrical Ballads}}'', London: J. & A. Arch, Part III, p. 17,<sup>[https://archive.org/details/lyricalballadswi00word]</sup>
#* {{RQ:Chesnutt House Behind the Cedars|chapter=I|page=10|passage=He walked slowly past the gate and '''peered''' through a narrow gap in the cedar hedge. The girl was moving along a sanded walk, toward a gray, unpainted house, with a steep roof, broken by dormer windows.}}
#* {{RQ:Burroughs Tarzan of the Apes|chapter=VI|page=65|passage=He would peek into the curtained windows, or, climbing upon the roof, '''peer''' down the black depths of the chimney in vain endeavor to solve the unknown wonders that lay within those strong walls.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[come]] [[in sight]]; to [[appear]].
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|act=IV|scene=iii|passage=And as the sun breaks through the darkest clouds, / So honour '''peereth''' in the meanest habit.}}
#* {{RQ:Jonson Catiline|sig=I|verso=1|sigend=I2|page=73|passage=I, I, let you alone, cunning Artificer! / See, hovv his gorget '''peeres''' aboue his govvne; / To tell the people, in vvhat danger he vvas.}}

===Etymology 2===
From {{inh|en|enm|per}}, {{m|enm|pere}}, from {{der|en|xno|peir}}, {{der|en|fro|per}}, from {{der|en|la|pār}}. {{doublet|en|pair|par}}.

====Pronunciation====

* {{enPR|pîr|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/pɪɹ/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-peer.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɪə(ɹ)|s=1}}
* {{homophones|en|pier}}

====Noun====
{{en-noun}}

# Somebody who is, or something that is, at a level or of a value equal (to that of something else).
#: {{syn|en|compeer}}
#* {{RQ:Dryden Fables|The Cock and the Fox
|passage=In song he never had his '''peer'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Isaac Taylor Saturday Evening|passage=Shall they draw off to their privileged quarters, and consort only with their '''peers'''?}}
# {{senseid|en|same age}} Someone who is approximately the same age (as someone else).
# {{senseid|en|Q7160407}} A noble with a title, i.e., a [[peerage]], and in times past, with certain rights and privileges not enjoyed by [[commoner]]s.
#: {{ux|en|a '''peer''' of the realm}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=Comus|passage=a noble '''peer''' of mickle trust and power}}
# A comrade; a companion; an associate.
#* {{RQ:Spenser Faerie Queene|book=I|canto=V|stanza=37|passage=He all his '''Peeres''' in beautie did surpas,}}

# To make equal in rank.
# {{lb|en|Internet}} To carry communications traffic terminating on one's own network on an equivalency basis to and from another network, usually without charge or payment. Contrast with ''[[transit]]'' where one pays another network provider to carry one's traffic.
